chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Hariz who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The one in a state of major impurity state massages (with oil), then washes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: The one in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah)
key_terms.قَالَ لَا: He said: No (indicating negation or confirmation of a specific ruling)

ai.seo_question: Does applying oil before ritual bath (ghusl) invalidate the purity for a person in major impurity (janub)?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of applying oil (*dahin*) prior to the ritual bath (*ghusl*) for one in a state of major impurity (*janub*). The Imam’s affirmative 'No' (negating the condition that it is impermissible or that it invalidates the bath) confirms that pre-bath oiling does not hinder the validity of *ghusl*, provided the water reaches the skin. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between mere surface coating and the actual obstruction of water flow during purification.
